newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers to continue strike Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers to continue strike Wednesday.

text.p: Brazil's National Portworkers Federation said it would extend its nationwide strike through Wednesday following the postponement of a vote on a Congressional bill regulating inland and coastal shipping.
"The strike is going to continue for at least another 24 hours," said Jose Renato Rosa, the federation's secretary general.

Portworkers began the strike at 0700 local/0900 GMT to protest changes introduced to the bill that would allow port operators to use non-union workers to handle cargo on ships traveling between Brazilian ports.
The stoppage reportedly halted activity at major Brazilian ports, including Santos, Brazil's largest port.

The bill was expected to be voted on today in the lower house of Congress, but its author Deputy Jose Carlos Aleluia said lawmakers would postpone the vote until Wednesday to allow last-minute changes.
Rosa said the strike was affecting all of Brazil's 32 ports and 60,000 portworkers.
These were the conditions at major Brazilian ports as of 1800 local/2000 gmt:

* Santos - The port is virtually stopped. There are 42 ships at the port, but only three ships containing chemcials and orange juice were loading and unloading. Cargo movement on ships carrying wheat and sugar has been halted.
* Vitoria - A spokesman was unavailable at 1800 local. At 1230 local, there were six ships at the port but only one ship carrying fruit was able to load.
* Paranagua - There was no movement of cargo on the eleven ships at the port.
* Rio de Janeiro - No information was available.
